text:
incident-bot: Pager — Elevated KV cache size and continuous-batching errors observed for NTK/YaRN sliding-window routes. autoclose in 2h unless acknowledged. metric: kv_cache_entries spike, downstream 5xx/429s increasing.

ravi (oncall): acked. joining bridge in 2. oncall: @alice @maggie can you jump? customers seeing tail latency spikes.

alice (eng-runtime): on it. initial glance: sliding-window prefix caches (NTK) saw cardinality explosion after the 03:00 model rollout — continuous batching holding many longctx pins. kv entries jumped ~10x in 15m.

maggie (sre): logs showing high eviction churn and OOM kill risk on rope-worker-3. p95 generation latency up from 220ms -> 2.4s. some upstream retries causing request amplification.

jon (platform): creating emergency tag and opening an infra bridge. link: https://zoom.redwood/infra-bridge-1791 (private).

carla (eng-ml): quick hypothesis: the new long-context window changed tokenization alignment for some prompts, causing the sliding-window key to vary more, reducing hit-rate and inflating KV set cardinality. continuous_batching holds KV items in memory during active sessions which compounds.

ravi (oncall): mitigation plan options: 1) short-term: disable sliding-window for NTK routes (config flip) or cap per-session KV entries; 2) revert continuous_batching config to conservative values; 3) route NTK traffic to smaller context variant (fallback). prefer minimal blast radius: try config flip first.

alice (eng-runtime): agreed. preparing hotfix: flip sliding_window.enabled -> false for model-group ntk-yarn-prod. will patch configmap and rollout to 20% pods, monitor.

alice (eng-runtime): applying patch now:

```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap model-ntk-yarn --patch 'data:{"sliding_window.enabled":"false","continuous_batch.max_inflight":"64"}'
```

maggie (sre): watching metrics: kv_cache_entries (global) 12.1M -> 9.2M, eviction_rate down slightly. p95 trending down. still seeing 429s from rate-limiter due to backlog.

ellie (customer-ops): heads up — AcmeAnalytics and BetaFin reported increased errors and delayed responses. I pinged both, letting them know we have an active mitigation and ETA ~15-30m. sharing any post-fix notes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

carla (eng-ml): also sending a quick rollback plan if flip causes regressions: we can set sliding_window.enabled=true and set continuous_batch.max_inflight=16, plus per-route kv_ttl=30s to bound growth.

alice (eng-runtime): hotfix rolled to 40% pods. quick perf snapshot: p95 -> 850ms, kv_entries -> 6.4M. traffic still being funneled to fallback in some regions.

ravi (oncall): good. start staged rollout to 100% if no regressions in 10m. also notify sales that we have mitigation in flight. @ellie can you update status page?

ellie (customer-ops): updating status.redwood.com: "Investigating — Elevated latencies for NTK sliding-window routes. Mitigation in progress." will send customer DM updates.

john (platform): (note) added temporary routing policy: route policy ntk-yarn -> fallback-ntk-compact for customers flagged as high-latency to reduce cost of retries.

maggie (sre): 10m after full rollout: kv entries stabilized ~3.1M, p95 ~300ms, errors down to baseline. no OOMs observed. setting alert thresholds to tighter values for the next 6h.

alice (eng-runtime): runbook actions executed: flipped sliding-window false, reduced continuous_batch.max_inflight, applied per-route kv_ttl=20s. snippet of config that landed:

```yaml
model_group: ntk-yarn-prod
sliding_window:
  enabled: false
continuous_batch:
  max_inflight: 64
kv_cache:
  per_session_ttl: 20s
```

ravi (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: high error rate and elevated latency for ~14 minutes pre-mitigation, affecting ~2% of requests on NTK routes; major customers: AcmeAnalytics (partial impact), BetaFin (delayed jobs). No data exfiltration.

ellie (customer-ops): AcmeAnalytics was told we expected full mitigation within 30m and follow-up report. BetaFin SLA hit will be logged; I requested case owners.

carla (eng-ml): follow-ups: longer-term fix options: 1) canonicalize sliding-window keys to reduce cardinality, 2) add adaptive per-session eviction based on ntk token distributions, 3) change batching heuristics to avoid huge in-flight KV retention for longctx sessions. I'll spin up an evaluation PR.

maggie (sre): handoff notes for next on-call (maggie -> jon at 18:00 UTC): watch kv_cache_entries, eviction_rate, continuous_batch.inflight_gauge, and rope-worker memory for 6h. alert if kv_cache_entries > 4M for > 10m.

alice (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a small dashboard with the key traces and add graphs to the incident issue.

ravi (oncall): thanks all. marking incident mitigation complete for now; will leave the incident thread open for postmortem drafting. @maggie you're the handoff owner. :white_check_mark:

maggie (sre): taking handoff. created incident issue: https://phabricator.redwood/INC-891 (draft). adding timeline + config diffs.

ellie (customer-ops): sending closure messages to impacted customers and scheduling follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated by maggie at 1791237890. next steps: postmortem in 48h, include root-cause analysis and a list of compensating controls.

maggie (sre): TL;DR for handoff ticket: NTK long-context changes increased sliding-window key variance -> KV cache cardinality blowup -> continuous-batching retention amplified memory use -> latency cliff and some 5xx/429s. Hotfix: disable sliding-window + cap continuous batching + per-session TTL. Owner: eng-runtime + eng-ml for durable fix.

carla (eng-ml): adding to my TODO: run offline sim to measure key cardinality change from rollout and propose canonicalization patch.

ravi (oncall): closing here. will re-open if anything spikes. good work everyone. :raised_hands:
